Author: T. Vinod Kumar
Bench: T. Vinod Kumar
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice T. Vinod Kumar
 Writ Petition No.20592 Of 2020
Order:

Heard learned Counsel for the petitioners, learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for respondent Nos.1 to 4 and Sri P. Sri Harsha Reddy, learned Standing Counsel appearing for respondent No.5 and perused the record.

2. Shorn of unnecessary details, the case of the petitioners in brief, is that the 1st and 3rd petitioners are the daughters of Kummari Balaiah and Akudari Parvatalu; that each of the petitioners father has been given laoni patta of the land to an extent of Ac.1.28 Gts. and Ac.4.00 Gts. in Sy. Nos.2/45 and 2/2 respectively; that the 2nd petitioner is a laoni patta holder of the land himself to an extent of Ac.2.30 Gts. in Sy. No.2/29 of Chopparipalli village of Bellampally Mandal; and that the petitioners are cultivating the aforesaid land which has been assigned in favour of original assignees.

3. Petitioners further contend that the respondent authorities are seeking to acquire the aforesaid extent of land assigned to the petitioners/their father for undertaking Open Cast Mining for the benefit of 5th respondent without following due process of law by initiating proceedings under Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013 as amended by Act 21 of 2017.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 4. Per contra, learned Government Pleader appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.1 to 4 submits that the authorities have only conducted a survey to identify the extent of land that is required to be acquired pursuant to a requisition from the 5th respondent and that in the event of the authorities initiating further action in respect of the aforesaid land, the authorities would follow due process of law.

5. Having regard to the submissions made as above, since it has been stated to this Court that in the event of the authorities requiring the aforesaid land which has been assigned to the petitioners'
father for respondent Nos.1 and 3 and to the 2nd petitioner, this Court is of the view that the respondent authorities are to be directed to follow due process of law by initiating proceedings for acquiring/resuming the aforesaid land by following due process of law under the Telangana Assigned Lands (Prohibition of Transfers) Act, 1977 and for providing Rehabilitation and Resettlement Package as per Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'Act 30 of 2013') as amended by Act 21 of 2017.
